title: Introduction and learning objectives
groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture and states what students should learn about cancer treatments.

title: Surgery and radiotherapy
groupedBecause: This subtopic explains local tumour treatment and how chemotherapy can support its effectiveness.

title: Cytotoxic chemotherapy
groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how conventional cytotoxic drugs work and what limits their clinical effectiveness.

title: Targeting hormone-dependent cancers
groupedBecause: This subtopic shows how blocking hormonal growth signals can selectively suppress hormone-dependent cancer cells.

title: Exploiting cancer cell checkpoint defects
groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how missing cell cycle checkpoints create vulnerabilities that treatments can exploit.

title: PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cancers
groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inhibiting PARP selectively kills cancer cells that cannot repair the resulting double-strand DNA breaks.

title: Oncogene addiction and targeted kinase inhibition
groupedBecause: These subtopics develop the rationale for identifying and inhibiting the activated oncogenic proteins on which tumours depend.

title: Kinase inhibitor resistance and long-term treatment limitations
groupedBecause: These subtopics examine why kinase inhibition often controls rather than cures cancer and how treatment must adapt to tumour resistance.

title: Antibody-directed cancer treatment
groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how antibodies recognise cancer cell surface proteins to direct therapeutic activity towards those cells.

title: Evidence for immune surveillance of cancer
groupedBecause: This subtopic evaluates whether the body's existing immune responses protect against cancer.

title: Immune checkpoint blockade and tumour recognition
groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how checkpoint blockade restores antitumour T cell activity and why tumour neoantigens influence its effectiveness.

title: Redirecting T cells towards cancer cells
groupedBecause: These subtopics describe engineered approaches that give T cells targeted access to cancer cells rather than relying on naturally occurring tumour recognition.

title: Treatment challenges and biomarker-guided therapy
groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how matching treatment to individual tumours can address the limitations of cancer therapy.

title: Cancer outcome trends, prevention and early detection
groupedBecause: This subtopic considers how prevention and earlier detection contribute to apparent improvements in cancer outcomes.

title: Future treatment priorities and ethical dilemmas
groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how future therapeutic progress must be weighed against established survival benefits and patients' quality of life.
